stem: Two elements $A$ and $B$ have similar chemical properties. They don't form solid hydrogencarbonates, but react with nitrogen to form nitrides. A and B, respectively, are:
solution:
Li and Mg do not form solid bicarbonate, but react with $\text{N}_2$ to give nitrides (diagonal relationship).

$6\text{Li} + \text{N}_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Li}_3\text{N}$

$3\text{Mg} + \text{N}_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$
subtopic: Diagonal relationship of Li and Mg

stem: For the reaction: $\text{NH}_3 + \text{OCl}^- \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{Cl}^-$ in basic medium, the coefficients of $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{OCl}^-$ and $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ for the balanced equation are respectively
$\text{PCl}_5$ is dissociating $50\%$ at $250^\circ$C at a total pressure of $P$ atm. If equilibrium constant is $K_p$, then which of the following relation is numerically correct -
solution:
$\text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2$

Moles at equilibrium: $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}$; mole fractions: $\frac{1}{3}$ each; partial pressures: $\frac{P}{3}$ each.

$$K_p = \frac{\frac{P}{3}\times\frac{P}{3}}{\frac{P}{3}} = \frac{P}{3} \Rightarrow P = 3K_p$$

stem: Work out the heat change (cal) when $40$ g of He gas at $27^\circ$C undergoes isothermal and reversible compression from initial pressure of $1$ atm to $10$ atm ($R = 2\ \text{cal K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$).
X mL of $\text{H}_2$ gas effuses through a hole in a container in $5$ seconds. The time taken for the effusion of the same volume of the gas specified below under identical conditions is:
Which of the following has minimum melting point?
solution:
Ionic compounds have high melting point. Greater the ionic character, more is the melting point. HCl is a covalent molecule with least ionic character among CsF, HCl, HF and LiF (and, unlike HF, no strong hydrogen bonding).

$\therefore$ HCl has minimum melting point.

stem: When $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$, $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ pass through a test tube which has ammonical $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$, find out which gas comes out unaffected from test tube?
solution:
$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ forms copper acetylide with ammonical $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$

$\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NH}_4\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$

$\text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \underset{\text{(copper acetylide)}}{\text{Cu}_2\text{C}_2} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Hence $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ and $\text{CH}_4$ come out unaffected.

stem: Fructose reduces Tollen's reagent due to:
options: enolisation of fructose followed by conversion to glucose (having aldehydic group) by the base present in Tollen's reagent
solution: In the alkaline medium of Tollen's reagent, fructose undergoes enolisation (Lobry de Bruyn–van Ekenstein rearrangement) to give glucose/mannose, which have a free aldehydic group and reduce Tollen's reagent.

stem: The solubility of silver bromide in hypo solution involves the formation of:
solution:
Hypo solution is $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ solution which is used in photography for fixing films & prints. Photographic emulsions are made of AgBr. After developing, the film is put into hypo solution. This forms soluble complex with Ag.

$\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{AgBr} \rightarrow \text{Ag}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3} \text{Na}_5[\text{Ag}(\text{S}_2\text{O}_3)_3]$
